findings.title: Existing V2 admin-permissions clients are never upgraded with the Clients schema
findings.body: `init` returns immediately whenever the admin-permissions client already exists. Realms that enabled FGAP V2 before this change therefore retain only the old Users scopes and resource-type resource; they never receive the Clients resource, nor configure/map-role client scopes. Creating a client permission in such a realm will fail while resolving missing scopes (and client authorization evaluation can reach a null all-clients resource). Initialization must reconcile/add newly introduced schema scopes and resource-type resources for an existing client, not only create them for a new client.

findings.title: V2 drops MANAGE_CLIENTS-role access for client role mapping
findings.body: The overrides for `canMapRoles`, `canMapCompositeRoles`, and `canMapClientScopeRoles` only evaluate an FGAP resource permission and do not preserve the `MANAGE_CLIENTS` admin-role shortcut used by the legacy evaluator. Consequently, when V2 is enabled, an administrator who has `realm-management`'s `manage-clients` role but no explicitly created authorization policy is denied client role assignment/composite/client-scope role mapping, even though the same role continues to authorize the other client-management operations. These methods need the equivalent root admin-role check (or delegation to the superclass) before FGAP evaluation.
